Jacques-Arsène d'Arsonval
Physician · Physicist · Inventor (France)
The Origin

History

The founder of this current is Jacques Arsène d'Arsonval, a famous doctor, but also a French physicist and inventor.

In 1890, Arsonval discovered the benefits of the permeability of plasma membrane by increasing frequency to more than 100 KHz. In the 1920s, with other researchers and doctors, he developed the first capacitive and resistive electrodes.

TECAR Therapy
Definition

What Is TECAR Therapy?

TECAR
Transferring Energy CАpacitive & Resistive
100+
kHz Frequency
0
Incisions

TECAR Therapy is a modern, non-invasive physiotherapy technique that uses high-frequency electromagnetic waves to treat muscular, joint, and skeletal injuries.

It's a form of deep thermal therapy that enhances blood circulation and stimulates the body's natural healing process by increasing internal tissue temperature.

03 / 14
TECAR Therapy
Two Modes

Capacitive & Resistive

C
Capacitive Mode
Targets soft tissues — muscles & tendons

Helps rapidly improve localised circulation, reduce muscle tension, and ease acute discomfort. Particularly effective for surface-level injuries and tissues that benefit from gentle, circulatory stimulation before deeper treatment is applied.

R
Resistive Mode
Reaches deep tissues — joints, ligaments, bone

CRET therapy in resistive mode generates a stronger thermal effect, stimulating cellular repair and reducing deep-seated inflammation. Commonly used for chronic joint conditions, ligament injuries, and musculoskeletal problems unresponsive to surface treatment alone.

Mechanism

How It Works

1
Radiofrequency

Utilizes radiofrequency waves between 300 kHz and 1.2 MHz

2

These waves penetrate deep into tissues, generating internal heat

3
Healing Response

Boosts cellular metabolism, reduces inflammation, and accelerates tissue repair

07 / 14
TECAR Therapy
Safety First

Contraindications

TECAR therapy should be avoided in the following cases:

!
Pregnancy — particularly abdominal & pelvic regions
!
Pacemakers or other implanted electronic devices
!
Over malignant tumors or cancerous areas
!
Active infections, especially in the treatment area
!
Thrombophlebitis or deep vein thrombosis (DVT)
!
Severe cardiovascular disorders
!
Sensitivity / allergy to electromagnetic fields
!
Metal, cement or plastic implants & piercings at the site
!
Orthodontic devices (for facial-area treatment)
08 / 14
TECAR Therapy
4–6
sessions for acute injuries
Treatment Plan

How many sessions are usually required?

The number of sessions depends on the condition and its severity. Acute injuries may respond within four to six sessions, while chronic conditions typically benefit from a longer course.
